newsitem.title: CHAD: IMF rewards Chad reforms with $11.4 million loan.
newsitem.headline: IMF rewards Chad reforms with $11.4 million loan.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund has given Chad a loan of 6.6 billion CFA francs ($11.4 million) after expressing satisfaction with progress on economic liberalisation, Chad's finance minister said on Sunday.

"During the IMF board meeting on June 13, the IMF administrators praised Chad's government for the progress made in the structural adjustment programme since 1995 and for their firm determination to push through economic reforms," Bichara Cherif Daoussa said in a statement.
"The IMF said it was encouraged by growth indicators in the different sectors of Chad's economy which demonstrate the sound basis of measures already taken to liberalise prices and trade," he added.
"Gross domestic product grew by 5.2 percent in real terms in 1994/95 and by six percent in 1996. Inflation has been brought under control," Bichara said, giving no further details.
The loan from the IMF is the second tranche of an enhanced structural adjustment facility.
The IMF noted the improvement in Chad's tax-gathering, Bichara said, but was worried about controls on spending, and especially on the government payroll.
The government has just ordered that allowances paid to civil servants and the military on top of salary be halved, and all new recruitment has been stopped for 1997.

The IMF has also called for further reforms to the banking sector, in particular the privatisation of the two banks still under state control, the Banque Tchadienne de Credit et de Depot (BTCD) and Banque de Developpement du Tchad (BDT).
